Apocalypdos

A mythic land where the fate of the world hangs in the balance.. every other week.

Layer
How to read: the outer rings are the fixed sky (15 gods, one 24-degree wedge and one 24-day month each). The disc beneath is the world, which turns once a year at 1 degree a day (with the Dial switch set to "sky turns", the world holds still and the sky rings turn instead). Each god has one high temple on the disc. It is marked on the map in its god's colour, and glows brightly when it passes under its own god and is joined to the god by a gold beam. That is the god's holy month, brightest on days 12 and 13. Press Play or drag the day slider.

Off. Heliax's wedge shows its own sun.

Centre = the great mountain at the middle of the island, balanced so the disc spins true. The violet haze on the rim is the Nyx pressing in; the motes are souls passing through. Temple positions are placed so that each temple meets its own god once a year, mid-month, which fits the 24-day months, one high temple per god, and "middle two days" peak.

How to read: pick a sort mode (season, A–Z, generation, closeness) and tap its picture to filter the cards. Tap a card to turn it over: the back shows both colours, symbol, personality, perception, generation and age; More opens the full detail below the cards (alignment, blessing, domains, race, ties, other forms and children, hook, temple). Colours are the sigil ring colours.

Popularity in general

The gods in order, most to least followed. Read: longer bar = more popular.

1. Luxys
2. Heliax
3. Arroas
4. Morgrim
5. Unitanya
6. Phaxes
7. Predalia
8. Havestra
9. Phurnos
10. Oceana
11. Thundros
12. Pharmika
13. Etheros
14. Necroxis
15. Kryonix

Why the list is in this order

Popularity is about fear, joy and daily routine, not about who is loved or good.

  • Luxys is first: everyone wants her favour to steer their fate somewhere better.
  • Heliax is the oaths-and-honour god and the literal sun, so people like him in general.
  • Morgrim is followed because 22 days of every year are guaranteed war, so you pray as hard as you can to the war god for a good outcome. Arroas sits a little above him because the Olympics are more entertaining and joyful than war.
  • Pharmika, Etheros and Necroxis are low because of the fear and discomfort around death.
  • Kryonix is unpopular among mortals because he is absent most of the year, but he is hugely popular on New Year’s Eve and is the only god worshipped in the Nyx plane at all. That does not lift his average, because far fewer people live in the Nyx.
  • The rest follow how often that god’s domain touches a mortal’s ordinary day.

Popularity is where belief is thin

Kryonix, Necroxis and Etheros are the least followed. Endless festivals and high holidays make fading very slim: so popularity changes how big the crowds are, not whether a god survives.

The idea cards

Birth sign and holy month

Everyone is born under a god's sky

Every wedge is inhabited, and everyone is born beneath one god's sky, a kind of astronomical birth sign. Each wedge honours the god above it, and each keeps a single high temple to a single god. When the god above and the temple below align, that is the god's holiest month, and worshippers flock to the temple on the middle two days. Months are 24 days, and the endless round of festivals and high holidays makes losing faith very unlikely.

  • The temple is the pilgrimage target because the world carries it under its god: the temple arrives, the pilgrims follow. With 15 wedges and 15 gods, one temple each, every god gets one holy month a year.
  • Birth sign equals birth date on the dial, so horoscopes double as calendar reading, and a Phaxes-born person has a born-under-a-liar's-sky reputation.
  • Two leaks for the titans: Heliax's holy month is the one where worship pours into a fake sun if Phaxes is covering, and Phaxes' own holy month is the one where he can't leave to cover. Both give a festival with a hidden cost.
  • The middle two days of a 24-day month are days 12 and 13, so the peak of the engine is a two-day window, 15 times a year.

Story seed: the year Heliax's temple month falls while Phaxes is the one in the sky.

Temples

One high temple per god, lesser sites everywhere

Each god has one high temple, and every wedge also keeps lesser places of worship for every god. Arroas may have a mega-Olympic stadium as his high temple, while every wedge has its own sports arenas.

  • Each god's worship takes the shape of their domain, so the high temple is the biggest version of a building type every wedge already has, and the lesser sites are daily-life infrastructure rather than shrines.
  • A wedge's character comes from the high temple it hosts: the Arroas wedge is a sports-mad culture all year, and the temple month is just the peak.
  • Travel and trade follow the holy months, so the pilgrimage seasons are the world's economy, which makes a stalled turn an economic collapse as well as a divine one.

Story seed: a wedge whose lesser arenas stay full all year, but whose high temple stands empty the month its god passes overhead.

How to read: what the shape of the world, the calendar and the peoples imply. Cards are labelled with the clue, the meaning, and a story seed.
Geography is theology

Your distance from the axis picks how you meet the gods

The wedges meet at an apex over the centre. Out at the rim each god swings overhead, large and sharp, once a year. Near the mountain all 15 crowd together and no one god ever dominates. So the rim has intense, seasonal, personal religion; the centre has the whole pantheon at once and a more administrative one.

Story seed: a rim priest sent to the centre cannot feel their god at all.

Navigation is politics

The sky is a map, so the Champions are infrastructure

Sailors steer by the fixed Champion constellations. Whoever gets a place in a god's mosaic becomes a landmark everyone depends on. Getting "put in the sky" is the biggest prize in the world, and someone decides who earns it.

Story seed: a navigator's guild that quietly lobbies which hero gets a star, because it keeps their trade routes working.

Frontier

The edge is the wild, the centre is civilisation

The rim freezes solid and the Nyx leaks in there; the centre is spared. That means magic, spirits, monsters and danger rise with distance from the mountain. Wealth, law and comfort sit inward.

Story seed: an expedition outward to a place where the dome meets the ground.

Reversal

The gods are fixed; the mortals are the ones in motion

A god's month is not the god travelling, it is the world arriving under them. Worship is the act of being carried into someone's presence. A month is a visit, not a visitation.

Story seed: a people who believe they are being carried away from a god they love.

Instrument

The calendar is a physical dial

Date equals angle, so anyone who can read the sky can read the day. The Champion constellations are not just a map, they are a clock face. Astronomers are timekeepers, and whoever controls the star charts controls the calendar and the festivals.

Still point

The mountain is the axle

The centre barely moves while the rim sweeps fastest, so the edge is wind, cold and speed, and the mountain is stillness and shade. It reads as the thing the world hangs on. Climbing it means leaving time behind.

Story seed: at the summit the year does not turn.

Institutionalised war

War has a season and a ceasefire

There is a fixed war month, a truce in the middle, and "slaughter resumes" after. So violence is scheduled, ritualised and taxed. Societies here have rules for fighting, which means they have rules for who gets to break them. Petty grievances between nearby communities often lead to skirmishes during this time. While Morgrim is watching, there is no room for negotiation, only dominance.

Story seed: a soldier who fights on a truce day.

Thresholds

The gaps between months are dangerous

Spirits slip through at midnight between months, and the year-turning (new years eve/day) is a Kryonix holy night. Every boundary is a door to what lies beyond. Superstitious people who care about safety plan around month-ends.

Civic life

There is a state, a budget and a vote

A financial year, a public debate and a prioritising vote, plus a sick count and open clinics.

Chicken and egg

Each race has a god, so who made whom?

Gods were born from collective belief. Every race pairs with a patron: lions and the sun, humans and fate, centaurs and the wild. Mortals created the gods that fit them, then the gods shaped the mortals back.

Ladder to heaven

Social rank ends in divinity

The power scale climbs from commoners through heroes and champions to royalty, saints and demi-gods. Social mobility here has a ceiling above humanity, which makes ambition a theological matter.

Family drama

The pantheon is a soap opera with consequences

Twin rivals, a groomed child, a toxic couple, a golden child. When gods fight, their devout fight for years. Faith wars are family feuds, scaled up.

With the flow, fate is with you

Those who sail with the flow of the world have fate with them; those who sail against it find fate turned against them too.

Oceana holds “Long Voyages & Change” and Luxys “Fate (Luck)”, and the Tidesturn hook already says sailors leave “with or against the flow of the world”. So the flow is the world's turn itself: the same magic that keeps the disc moving also leans luck toward whoever moves the same way. Going against it is going against the Gods' will.

Why it fits: it makes the turn felt by ordinary people, not just the gods, and it gives the navigator's guild a real product: a rota of favourable crossings.

Story seed: a captain who deliberately sails against the flow to prove fate is a story, and the crew who quietly stop believing in her luck.

The Nyx

A dreamy plane of cosmic-aurora magic where the powers of potentiality and belief hold sway: the realm of god-like magic, belief given form, of dreams, fears and shifting philosophies.
Kalashtar are Nyx-touched humans.
The Nyxian are Nyx-born people; Fae (elves), Daemons (tieflings) and half-half are called “Faelings”.

Dragonborn are literally the children of dragons

Life stages, in order:Hatchling infancy · 5e: kobold
The smallest and most protected stage.Dragonfolk pre-puberty · 5e: lizardfolk
Still growing into their strength, they play at the contests they will one day live for.Dragonborn puberty
Dragons are apex predators, so Dragonborn love competition above all.Young Dragon adolescence
Dragonborn grow wings as they enter adolescence, then take to the skies to test the skills they honed on the ground.Adult Dragon adulthood
Builds a hoard and raises hatchlings. Killing an Adult Dragon (or younger) is considered murder.Ancient Dragon twilight years
Past the reproductive stage and arrogant with wealth and power. Can be ethically hunted for its hoard.

Lizardfolk side branch, from Dragonborn · 5e: kobold / lizardfolk
The mixed-blood children of Dragonborn who cannot mature into puberty. Seen as impure and not worthy of Arroas, they are often killed at birth and are therefore even rarer than Dragonborn.

Story seed: a dragonfolk cult that insists it is a larval stage and wants to grow up.

The Ephorgy (Warforged)

Built for Unitanya as a gift to Morgrim, so he could wage wars without pointless pain and death. Morgrim refused: without pain, the constructs gave him no satisfaction. So the Ephorgy, built to obey orders, became civil servants, labourers and factory workers who act tirelessly; sentient but distinctly artificial. They often act as simple marble statues until needed.

Story seed: they are counted among Phurnos' children, yet Unitanya commissioned them: whose faith do they carry?

The Djinn (Genasi)

Thundros inspired Phurnos to build a new kind of Ephorgy that could live freely in sea and sky, like his beloved Harpies. Phurnos made the first biological artificial lifeforms: the Storm Djinn [air & water genasi]. Phurnos was so pleased with the results that he made Volcano Djinn [earth & fire genasi] in his own image. A Volcanic-Storm Djinn (extremely rare) is hailed as a champion of both Gods, expected to have a great destiny.

Story seed: a Volcanic-Storm Djinn born on a day Thundros and Phurnos are both under sky.

Minotaurs build the labyrinths

Phurnos tasked the minotaurs to build the labyrinths as gates for the permanent openings to the Nyx.

How to read: plain lines are what everyone is told. Trusted lines are truths mortals are never told, Gods-only lines are what the gods keep to themselves, and Rumour lines are market tales, never the whole truth. The same lines appear under each god (Lore and rumours) and in Holy months (Festival tales). Use the Layer row at the top to open the Trusted and Gods-only layers, and the search box to find a tale.

Glitch reread

Phaxes' month is where the turntable stutters

A smooth rotation would give clean seasons. His month shifts weather and season at will, so it fits a stumble in the turn, the wobble the other gods cover for. The liar is hiding a mechanical fault.

Patchwork world

Everything divine is a repair job

The sun is injured, so the moon was made to cover the night. Time had to be spun and woven just to hold the world together. The pantheon reads less like rulers and more like survivors holding a leaking roof.

Story seed: something is wearing through, and the gods are hiding how fast.

Missing god

Kryonix is probably spent

The weapon "would certainly kill him", he is rarely seen, and he only appears on the last night of the year. The most likely reading is that he is diminished or half-dead, kept alive by the year turning. Nobody knows why he is absent, so someone is not telling.

Story seed: on the last night he appears, and he is wrong in a way only one character notices.

Dark reading

The dead feed the machine

Souls stream back into the Nyx to be reincarnated at once, with déjà vu as the leak. That is efficient, and a little horrifying: the afterlife is a recycling line, and the gods draw on what it carries.

Story seed: someone remembers a past life clearly, and a god wants to know why.

Glitch month

Phaxes' month is the calendar's safety valve

360 days exactly, no leap day, and one month with no fixed season. The trickster's month is where the world's slop gets absorbed. The liar covers the maths error.

Loose threads

Threads the world has not tied off.

Sara Toga

A figure named Sara Toga, known only by name.

Story seed: a toga-clad Luxys-girl aspect (her girl-in-a-toga form) who is, or thinks she is, a mortal.

The child who ends the world

A child prophesied to end the world. If this child embraces Death, Death will embrace us all.

Story seed: Necroxis is "Acceptance", and the engine only turns while souls cycle on; a child who accepts death could stop souls re-entering the cycle.

Who is hurt by Heliax's gaze?

No one has said.

Story seed: Heliax's "injury" and the sun-for-a-head: his gaze burns, so the hidden half-day is also a mercy to someone.

How to read: everything that is not about one god: creation, the Nyx, titans, the master lists, power scale and notes. Use the buttons to jump.

Creation

Before the beginning, Kryonix and Luxys were the only Gods. Companions, lovers, rivals. They explored the chaotic Cosmos together, battling intelligent Titans of Arcana and primal Titans of the Elements for domination. Their goal; To bring balance to the Cosmos.

Kryonix searched every horizon of the Cosmos for a weapon that could turn the tide of the war in their favor. He learned that such a weapon could be created but that the effort would certainly kill him, so he asked Luxys to bolster his strength with her own divine energies. Trusting him completely, they temporarily merged themselves together to become a single entity, known as Luxonix.

Unified as one, they infused raw Cosmic energy with their own divine power and created the Nyx, a substance that can amplify the power of belief into pure divine energy and bring order to chaos. Successful in their goal but weakened and separated once again, the two Gods were vulnerable and alone. To protect the Nyx from the Titans and the chaos of the Cosmos, the Gods needed a place to safely cultivate the Nyx.

Looking for guidance and using the power of the Nyx, Kryonix spun the concept of time into threads and Luxys wove those threads into The Tapestry of Fate, that spans the entire cosmos. Their first interpretation of the Tapestry was that the Mortal World was always meant to exist as a safe place for the Nyx.. and so it did, thanks to the power of the God's belief and the Nyx.

As the Nyx spread across the world, mortal beings began feeding the Nyx with their dreams and superstitions. Which soon resulted in a new generation of Gods being born. These Gods represented the earliest mortal's divine beliefs in; Nature/Life, Death, the Sun, the Ocean, and Fire. These Gods were the first to interact directly with the mortal world to encourage belief and teach mortals of their cosmic struggle.

Over time, a third generation of Gods manifested from the collective beliefs and structures of early mortal society. The first Competition was the struggle to survive. The desperation within that struggle breeds War and war creates a lot of resentful Spirits. Scattered Farming villages that necessitated the first Trade Networks. Networks that expanded to the sea, where success was dictated by knowledge of the sky, the ocean and the Weather. With the import of resources comes better nutrition, longer lifespans and access to exotic medicines. Also with trade comes stories, of mythical far off places and creatures, but also greed and with greed, lies. As such, these new Gods came to be the final members of the Pantheon that protect the World from the Cosmos that surrounds it. They use mortal belief to fuel their efforts to subdue the Titans and bring order to the Cosmos.

The Nyx and the Faelings

Elves ("Fae"), Tieflings ("daemons") and their mixed-bloods are now called FAELINGS, a name that sounds like "failings". Faelings are extremely rare, because fae and daemons mix badly, both socially and biologically. The name replaces "Elflings".

To ordinary mortals all three read as "Nyx-born", but the true Nyx-born are mortals who live in, or come from, the Nyx. They are tied to Kryonix, who spends most of his time there, and most of them never cross to the mortal plane.

The Nyx holds a limbo-like plane where time and space are "wibbly-wobbly": a hyper-magical version of the mortal plane. It is the substance the world was made from, and the river of souls runs through it. It touches the afterlife plane and the mortal plane equally, though it reaches the afterlife more easily.

Notes

  • 1 yr = 15 mths w/ 24 d/ea = 360 d/yr
  • This is a disc-world, where the Sun rises and sets in the same position in the sky every day as the world rotates. Each day is a single degree of the 360 degree axis. The sun moves with Heliax's wedge through the year.
  • The sky is segmented into 15 tall triangles that converge into a dome that covers the World. Each segment is a mosaic of star constellations and nebulae, representative of a single God and their most honoured Champions. The closer you are to a God's segment, the more they come into focus until you can see them in high definition, framed by their Champion mosaic. Behind them the Cosmos can be seen, chaotically changing over the eons. Planets can be seen independantly moving through space, stars dissapear randomly and pieces of debris can often be seen burning away across the dome before they reach the World (a bunch of meteors hitting the dome directly would be like fireworks.. very cool). Navigators must use the fixed position of the Champion constellations to move through the World.
  • To the mortals, the seasons and sky rotate around the world, but in reality it's the world that is spinning.
